title: HTRANS: Accepted Beats, Waits, BUSY, and Illegal Termination
description: Follow an INCR4 burst whose accepted-beat counter advances only on HREADY-high NONSEQ/SEQ edges, then compare a SINGLE-to-BUSY violation and early termination of a fixed-length burst.

annotations.message: The INCR4 NONSEQ beat is accepted because HREADY is HIGH; accepted-beat count becomes one.
The SEQ address 0x104 is visible but HREADY is LOW, so it is pending and the count remains one.
The held 0x104 SEQ beat is now accepted. The buggy SINGLE sequence, by contrast, already violated the rule by inserting BUSY after its sole beat.
BUSY preserves the valid INCR4 context but consumes no beat and does not itself guarantee arbitration ownership.
The third accepted INCR4 beat advances the count. The buggy INCR4 terminates here after only two accepted beats.
The fourth accepted beat legally completes the fixed-length INCR4 burst. An undefined-length INCR can instead terminate after BUSY at a permitted boundary, but still cannot cross 1 KB.

violations.message: SINGLE cannot continue with BUSY; the single accepted NONSEQ beat already completed that burst.
The fixed-length INCR4 burst terminates after only two accepted beats; wait and BUSY cycles never count as beats.
